## 1. Sri Lanka’s consumer inflation rose to 6.8% year-on-year in June, the highest in three years, according to the Colombo Consumer Price Index.

The index (a basket-based measure of prices in Greater Colombo) accelerated from 5.5% in May as energy and food costs climbed. <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Core inflation edged up to 4.0%</span>, suggesting underlying price pressures persisted.

The print came as the central bank’s 5% target band was already breached after a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">100-basis-point rate hike</span> in May. Officials said inflation would stay above target near term before easing toward mid‑2027 if policy discipline holds.

## 2. An IMF mission concluded a week-long staff visit to Colombo after reviewing reform progress under the Extended Fund Facility.

The programme (a multi-year balance‑of‑payments support arrangement) will next be formally assessed at the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Seventh Review expected in September</span>. Staff noted robust tax receipts and activity despite Middle East spillovers, while cautioning that sustained reforms remain critical.

The Fund cited higher energy costs and softer tourism as headwinds but said revenue outturns had been <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">broad‑based</span>. Authorities reiterated commitment to a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">2.3% of GDP primary surplus</span> by 2027 and to completing remaining structural benchmarks.

## 3. The Asian Development Bank approved a $200 million emergency loan to support post‑Cyclone Ditwah reconstruction.

The package covered road and irrigation rehabilitation, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">owner‑driven housing grants</span> and farmer support, with a $500,000 technical assistance grant attached. Disbursements will apply “<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">build back better</span>” standards to harden assets against future climate shocks.

The facility follows widespread damage across <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">22 districts</span> and aims to restore about 31.8 million kWh equivalent in system productivity through asset repairs. The project is expected to reduce annual carbon emissions versus pre‑event baselines by improving network efficiency.

## 4. The Government said the state of emergency imposed after Cyclone Ditwah will lapse at the end of this month.

Officials stated the regulation was used to expedite disaster recovery works and would <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">not be extended</span>. The announcement followed Cabinet briefings that linked the rule strictly to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">reconstruction needs</span> rather than security policy.

Ministers said normal administrative law would govern remaining works and procurements. Agencies were instructed to continue inter‑institutional coordination under <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">existing statutes</span>.

## 5. Sri Lanka’s current account posted a $194.5 million deficit in May as the merchandise trade gap nearly doubled year-on-year.

Imports rose <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">45.4% to $2.19 billion</span> while exports increased 18.3% to $1.22 billion, widening the goods deficit to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$967.9 million</span>. Reserves stood at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$6.9 billion</span> at end‑May after IMF disbursements, external debt service and net foreign‑exchange sales by the central bank.

## 6. President Anura Kumara Dissanayake appointed Duminda Hulangamuwa as Chairman of the Board of Investment.

The new board includes Vish Govindasamy, Harshani Randiligama, Mangala Karunaratne and K.A. Vimalenthirarajah. The agency said it would restore <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">one‑stop investor services</span> and accelerate project pipelines to narrow the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">structural trade deficit</span>.

## 7. Vietjet opened bookings for the first direct Colombo–Ho Chi Minh City flights starting 18 August 2026.

The route will operate <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">three round trips weekly</span> with one‑way Eco fares from <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$90 all‑in</span>. The carrier said the five‑hour sector enables onward connectivity across Asia‑Pacific through its network hub.

## 8. Sri Lanka’s dengue caseload exceeded 55,000 by end‑June, with that month alone accounting for 21,565 infections.

The <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Western Province</span> reported over half of total cases, while <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">32 deaths</span> were recorded so far this year. Health authorities said June’s surge reflected intensified rainfall and urged continuous source reduction beyond one‑off clean‑ups.

## 9. The Cabinet cleared the Rabies Eradication and Dog Registration Bill for publication and tabling in Parliament.

The draft consolidates legacy ordinances, mandates <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">vaccination and legal registration</span>, and defines institutional powers for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">enforcement</span>. Officials said the measure targets nationwide dog‑population control and improved <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">public‑health surveillance</span>.

## 10. Water tariffs will remain unchanged for the next six months, the Housing, Construction and Water Supply Minister said.

The decision follows the utility’s <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">lower-than-expected treatment costs</span> in the first half. Officials added that a further freeze is possible pending cost reviews typically conducted <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">semiannually</span>.
